boundary_rationale: The span opens the part on a reign-change notice, וַיִּ֨מְלָךְ מֶ֔לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ בֶּן יֹֽאשִׁיָּ֑הוּ תַּ֗חַת כָּנְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן יְה֣וֹיָקִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִמְלִ֛יךְ נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל בְּאֶ֥רֶץ יְהוּדָֽה (oshb:Jer.37.1, byte), matching “Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigned as king instead of Coniah the son of Jehoiakim, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king in the land of Judah.” (web:Jer.37.1) — the bytes name the new king’s predecessor כָּנְיָ֨הוּ֙ (Konyahu, byte; oshb:Jer.37.1), the Coniah form, one of three name forms this king carries across the book (sweep: 3 verses); the reign's installer carries no further identification beyond the royal title, “whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made king” (web:Jer.37.1), the resh-family spelling נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּ֥ר standing in the same clause (oshb:Jer.37.1, byte). Verse 2 continues the same notice with a general character report, וְלֹ֥א שָׁמַ֛ע ה֥וּא וַעֲבָדָ֖יו וְעַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ אֶל דִּבְרֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִֽיא (oshb:Jer.37.2, byte), matching “But neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land, listened to Yahweh's words, which he spoke by the prophet Jeremiah.” (web:Jer.37.2) — naming the king, his servants, and the people of the land together, a summary claim about the reign rather than a dated scene. The inventory’s own setumah sits at oshb:Jer.36.32 (single-witness WLC archival, weak, tier-3 corroboration, governed by the Prophets addendum), immediately before this span’s own front seam; no mark falls inside verses 1-2 themselves.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding these two verses into the embassy scene that follows as one larger opening unit was rejected because verses 1-2 report the reign and a general hearing failure as a summary notice, while verse 3 turns to the narrated sending of named envoys carrying a specific request, וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֜הוּ (oshb:Jer.37.3, byte).
literature_type_guess: regnal succession notice with a summary disobedience report
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The clause naming Zedekiah's accession is itself the seam the part opens on, a reign change standing in for a dated formula at the head of a new narrative stretch. The predecessor's name appears here in its Coniah form; the book's other two forms for the same king, Jehoiachin and Jeconiah, belong to other chapters and are not engaged by this span. Nebuchadnezzar's resh-family spelling recurs through the chapters ahead (sweep: 29 verses), with a plene byform at Jer.49.28; the book also carries a nun-family spelling elsewhere (sweep: 6 verses), including a vav-less defective form at Jer.28.11 and Jer.28.14, none attested in this span.

boundary_rationale: A named embassy opens the scene, matching “Zedekiah the king sent Jehucal the son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah, the priest, to the prophet Jeremiah, saying,” (web:Jer.37.3), asking him to pray to Yahweh their God on their behalf — Zedekiah sending two officials to ask Jeremiah to pray; a petuchah closes this opening notice at oshb:Jer.37.5 (single-witness WLC; Prophets tier-3, weak corroboration), keying the junction immediately before the oracle's own onset, the notice that Pharaoh's army had left Egypt, וְחֵ֥יל פַּרְעֹ֖ה יָצָ֣א מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וַיִּשְׁמְע֨וּ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֜ים הַצָּרִ֤ים עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ אֶת שִׁמְעָ֔ם וַיֵּ֣עָל֔וּ מֵעַ֖ל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם (oshb:Jer.37.5, byte). The prophetic answer to that same embassy is framed by its own word-event notice, וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל יִרְמְיָ֥הוּ הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.37.6, byte), matching “Then Yahweh’s word came to the prophet Jeremiah, saying,” (web:Jer.37.6), and opens with כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.37.7, byte) — “Yahweh, the God of Israel, says” (web:Jer.37.7) — the divine formula, its mouth named as Yahweh answering the king's own messengers rather than any other speaker. A setumah closes the oracle's first turn at oshb:Jer.37.8 (single-witness WLC evidence, weak, tier-3 corroboration), וְשָׁ֨בוּ֙ הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים וְנִלְחֲמ֖וּ עַל הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֑את וּלְכָדֻ֖הָ וּשְׂרָפֻ֥הָ בָאֵֽשׁ (oshb:Jer.37.8, byte), before the reply continues through the Chaldeans' certain return in verses 9-10.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the word-event onset at verse 6 away from the embassy's request in verses 3-5 into two rows was rejected because the oracle directly answers the same messengers named in verse 3, with no addressee change between the request and the reply.
literature_type_guess: royal embassy's request for intercession answered by a dated military oracle
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: A ketiv/qere note stands at MT 37:4, the unpointed written form beside the pointed read form, הכליא הַכְּלֽוּא (oshb:Jer.37.4, byte; single-witness apparatus), present in the span though not engaged by this row's prose. The word-event formula at verse 6 belongs to the book's vayehi-debar-YHWH shape, one of three disjoint shapes the byte-derived census carries book-wide — vayehi-debar-YHWH at 21 verses, the prose-sermon superscription at 11, and the OAN/topical header at 4, no verse shared between them. A paseq also stands in verses 7 and 9 (single-witness here — a seg-layer, count-only disclosure; no position is claimed for either).

boundary_rationale: The scene turns to Jeremiah's own movement once the siege lifts, וְהָיָ֗ה בְּהֵֽעָלוֹת֙ חֵ֣יל הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים מֵעַ֖ל יְרֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם מִפְּנֵ֖י חֵ֥יל פַּרְעֹֽה (oshb:Jer.37.11, byte), matching “When the army of the Chaldeans had withdrawn from Jerusalem for fear of Pharaoh's army,” (web:Jer.37.11); a setumah marks this same verse in the inventory (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration), texture at the turn rather than its warrant. He is seized at Benjamin's gate on a charge of desertion and brought before the officials, matching “When he was in Benjamin's gate, a captain of the guard was there, whose name was Irijah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Hananiah; and he seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "You are defecting to the Chaldeans!"” (web:Jer.37.13); the officials strike him and hold him in Jonathan the scribe's house, matching “The princes were angry with Jeremiah, and struck him, and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the scribe; for they had made that the prison.” (web:Jer.37.15). A petuchah closes the span at oshb:Jer.37.16 (single-witness WLC attestation, weak, tier-3 corroboration), כִּ֣י בָ֧א יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ אֶל בֵּ֥ית הַבּ֖וֹר וְאֶל הַֽחֲנֻ֑יוֹת וַיֵּֽשֶׁב שָׁ֥ם יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ יָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים (oshb:Jer.37.16, byte), where Jeremiah is reported to have remained many days.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the seizure at the gate from the imprisonment that follows into two rows was rejected because no formula, addressee change, or dated notice interrupts the single chain from seizure to the many days in the cells.
literature_type_guess: departure, seizure, and initial imprisonment narrative
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The captain who seizes Jeremiah is identified by a three-generation line ending in a Hananiah, בֶּן חֲנַנְיָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.37.13, byte); this is Irijah's grandfather, a different bearer of the name from the prophet of chapter 28. Jonathan the scribe is named as the owner of the house turned prison, a detail the plea in the following span returns to by name.

boundary_rationale: A petuchah closes the preceding span at oshb:Jer.37.16 (single-witness WLC reading, weak, tier-3 corroboration) immediately before a fresh royal action opens this one, וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֜הוּ וַיִּקָּחֵ֗הוּ (oshb:Jer.37.17, byte), matching “then Zedekiah the king sent and had him brought out. The king asked him secretly in his house,” (web:Jer.37.17) — Zedekiah sending for Jeremiah privately, distinct from the officials' custody just closed. A setumah also marks this same verse, oshb:Jer.37.17 (single-witness WLC surviving, weak, tier-3 corroboration, governed by the Prophets addendum). Jeremiah's own plea follows, matching “Now please hear, my lord the king: please let my supplication be presented before you, that you not cause me to return to the house of Jonathan the scribe, lest I die there.” (web:Jer.37.20) — addressed to the king with אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.37.20, byte), the human “my lord” used of a king rather than the distinct divine-title pointing of the same three consonants, asking not to be returned to Jonathan's house. The king answers by committing him instead to the court of the guard, matching “Then Zedekiah the king commanded, and they committed Jeremiah into the court of the guard. They gave him daily a loaf of bread out of the bakers’ street, until all the bread in the city was gone. Thus Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard.” (web:Jer.37.21), closing the span on that outcome.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying the transfer notice in verse 21 forward into the officials' scene that opens chapter 38 was rejected because verse 21 completes and closes the private audience begun at verse 17, while the next span opens on a different, named set of officials.
literature_type_guess: secret royal audience and transfer to the court of the guard
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: A ketiv/qere note stands at MT 37:19, the unpointed written form beside the pointed read form, ואיו וְאַיֵּה֙ (oshb:Jer.37.19, byte; single-witness apparatus), present in the span though not engaged by this row's prose. The vocative opening Jeremiah's plea at verse 20, אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.37.20, byte), is pointed as the human my-lord form addressed to the king, not the distinct divine-title pointing of the same three consonants; the same human form recurs in the cistern-rescue scene ahead. Jeremiah asks by name not to die in Jonathan the scribe's house, the very house named as his earlier prison in the preceding span.

boundary_rationale: A new set of four named officials opens the span, וַיִּשְׁמַ֞ע שְׁפַטְיָ֣ה בֶן מַתָּ֗ן וּגְדַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן פַּשְׁח֔וּר וְיוּכַל֙ בֶּן שֶׁ֣לֶמְיָ֔הוּ וּפַשְׁח֖וּר בֶּן מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה אֶ֨ת הַדְּבָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֧ר יִרְמְיָ֛הוּ מְדַבֵּ֥ר אֶל כָּל הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), matching “Shephatiah the son of Mattan, Gedaliah the son of Pashhur, Jucal the son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur the son of Malchijah heard the words that Jeremiah spoke to all the people, saying,” (web:Jer.38.1); a setumah marks this same verse, oshb:Jer.38.1 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration). Jeremiah's own proclamation to the people opens with its koh-amar frame, כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ (oshb:Jer.38.2, byte), matching “Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.38.2), continuing at הַיֹּשֵׁב֙ בָּעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את יָמ֕וּת בַּחֶ֖רֶב בָּרָעָ֣ב וּבַדָּ֑בֶר (oshb:Jer.38.2, byte; a ketiv/qere note also sits later in this verse, not engaged by this splice) — matching “He who remains in this city will die by the sword, by the famine, and by the pestilence,” (web:Jer.38.2); a further setumah falls at this same verse, oshb:Jer.38.2. A second koh-amar frame follows, כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.38.3, byte), matching “Yahweh says,” (web:Jer.38.3) — relaying that the city will surely be given into the hand of the king of Babylon's army, who will take it — both frames the words Jeremiah, per oshb:Jer.38.1, was himself speaking to all the people. The officials petition the king that Jeremiah be put to death for weakening the soldiers' resolve, matching “Then the princes said to the king, "Please let this man be put to death, because he weakens the hands of the men of war who remain in this city, and the hands of all the people, in speaking such words to them; for this man doesn't seek the welfare of this people, but harm."” (web:Jer.38.4); Zedekiah answers that he is in their hand, matching “Zedekiah the king said, "Behold, he is in your hand; for the king can't do anything to oppose you."” (web:Jer.38.5), and they cast him into Malchijah's cistern, וַיִּקְח֣וּ אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ וַיַּשְׁלִ֨כוּ אֹת֜וֹ אֶל הַבּ֣וֹר מַלְכִּיָּ֣הוּ בֶן הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אֲשֶׁר֙ בַּחֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָ֔ה וַיְשַׁלְּח֥וּ אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בַּחֲבָלִ֑ים וּבַבּ֤וֹר אֵֽין מַ֨יִם֙ כִּ֣י אִם טִ֔יט וַיִּטְבַּ֥ע יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ בַּטִּֽיט (oshb:Jer.38.6, byte), where a third setumah closes the span at this same verse, oshb:Jer.38.6 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the officials' petition to the king in verses 4-6 away from what they heard in verses 1-3 was considered, since the address moves from the people generally to the king by name; it is rejected because no fresh introductory formula marks that turn, only the ordinary narrative chain continuing from what was just heard to what was then done about it.
literature_type_guess: officials' complaint against Jeremiah and his casting into the cistern
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: Two of the four officials named at verse 1 carry patronymics built on Pashhur — Gedaliah son of Pashhur, and Pashhur son of Malchijah in his own right, distinct from Gedaliah son of Ahikam named later in these chapters. The full name-plus-patronymic of this second Pashhur, וּפַשְׁח֖וּר בֶּן מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), is not unique to this span: the identical form, פַּשְׁחוּר֙ בֶּן מַלְכִּיָּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.21.1, byte), stands at that site, so the full patronymic joins the two rather than separating them, and the disambiguation the bytes actually supply is against the priest Pashhur of chapter 20, whose own patronymic differs entirely. Conversely, the embassy member named at oshb:Jer.37.3 as יְהוּכַ֣ל בֶּן שֶֽׁלֶמְיָ֗ה stands here as וְיוּכַל֙ בֶּן שֶׁ֣לֶמְיָ֔הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), both the given name and the patronymic differing in form between the two sites, so matching by full patronymic would wrongly split one man into two. The span itself splices two spellings of the name Malchijah under one English name: מַלְכִּיָּ֑ה (oshb:Jer.38.1, byte), the father of the fourth official, against מַלְכִּיָּ֣הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.6, byte), the king's son whose cistern receives Jeremiah — the longer form the only such spelling of the name in the book (sweep: 1 verse). Two paseq segs stand at oshb:Jer.38.4 and one at oshb:Jer.38.6 (single-witness testimony: seg layer, count-only reporting; no position is claimed for any).

boundary_rationale: Ebedmelech the Ethiopian opens a rescue scene once the setumah closing the preceding span at oshb:Jer.38.6 (single-witness WLC notice, weak, tier-3 corroboration) gives way to וַיִּשְׁמַ֡ע עֶֽבֶד מֶ֨לֶךְ הַכּוּשִׁ֜י אִ֣ישׁ סָרִ֗יס וְהוּא֙ בְּבֵ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּֽי נָתְנ֥וּ אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ אֶל הַבּ֑וֹר וְהַמֶּ֥לֶךְ יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּשַׁ֥עַר בִּנְיָמִֽן (oshb:Jer.38.7, byte), matching “Now when Ebedmelech the Ethiopian, a eunuch, who was in the king’s house, heard that they had put Jeremiah in the dungeon (the king was then sitting in Benjamin’s gate),” (web:Jer.38.7). He appeals to the king directly, matching “My lord the king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, whom they have cast into the dungeon. He is likely to die in the place where he is, because of the famine; for there is no more bread in the city.” (web:Jer.38.9) — opening אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ (oshb:Jer.38.9, byte), the same human vocative used of Zedekiah earlier in these chapters rather than a divine title — and the king commands the rescue, וַיְצַוֶּ֣ה הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֛ת עֶֽבֶד מֶ֥לֶךְ הַכּוּשִׁ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר קַ֣ח בְּיָדְךָ֤ מִזֶּה֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים אֲנָשִׁ֔ים וְֽהַעֲלִ֜יתָ אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֧הוּ הַנָּבִ֛יא מִן הַבּ֖וֹר בְּטֶ֥רֶם יָמֽוּת (oshb:Jer.38.10, byte). Ebedmelech gathers rags and cords — the very token carrying the span's one ketiv/qere note at oshb:Jer.38.11 — and carries out that command; a setumah closes the span at oshb:Jer.38.13 (single-witness WLC deposition, weak, tier-3 corroboration) as Jeremiah returns to the court of the guard, matching “So they lifted Jeremiah up with the cords, and took him up out of the dungeon; and Jeremiah remained in the court of the guard.” (web:Jer.38.13).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the king's command in verse 10 away from Ebedmelech's own performance in verses 11-13 was rejected because a command carried out without an intervening formula, addressee change, or dated notice stands as one unit under the ruled granularity.
literature_type_guess: Ebedmelech's rescue of Jeremiah from the cistern
wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
device_notes: The rescue is staged at the king's own house, under the treasury, before returning Jeremiah to the same court of the guard named at the close of the preceding span; the location and the custodial term both carry forward rather than reset. A ketiv/qere note stands at oshb:Jer.38.11, the unpointed written form beside the pointed read form, הסחבות סְחָב֔וֹת (single-witness apparatus); a paseq also stands at this same verse (single-witness only, this is a seg-layer count, nothing more; no position claimed).

boundary_rationale: A setumah closes the rescue span at oshb:Jer.38.13 (single-witness WLC evidence, weak, tier-3 corroboration) immediately before the king reopens contact on his own initiative, וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּ֗הוּ וַיִּקַּ֞ח אֶֽת יִרְמְיָ֤הוּ הַנָּבִיא֙ אֵלָ֔יו אֶל מָבוֹא֙ הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ שֹׁאֵ֨ל אֲנִ֤י אֹֽתְךָ֙ דָּבָ֔ר אַל תְּכַחֵ֥ד מִמֶּ֖נִּי דָּבָֽר (oshb:Jer.38.14, byte), matching “Then Zedekiah the king sent and took Jeremiah the prophet to himself into the third entry that is in Yahweh’s house. Then the king said to Jeremiah,” (web:Jer.38.14) — a new location, the temple's third entry, and a demand that Jeremiah hide nothing from him. Jeremiah's wary reply opens verse 15; the king's sworn oath follows, and a further setumah is marked at that same verse, oshb:Jer.38.16 (single-witness WLC; weak, tier-3 corroboration).
